paper.title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
paper.abstract: The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars. This is theorized to happen via Common Envelope Evolution (CEE), when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here, we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, that originates from the CEE of a ~7M$_{\odot}$ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as a ~0.7M$_{\odot}$ companion inspiraling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven year period of gradual brightening - the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core within a few (<10) orbits powers the ejection of the outermost ~10% of the stellar envelope at speeds ~10x the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope, $0.01\lesssim α\lesssim 0.4$. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.

paper.title: Algorithmic List Decoding at Capacity and Optimal Proximity Gaps for Reed-Solomon Codes
paper.abstract: We give a unified hidden-derivative framework for list decoding and mutual correlated agreement of ordinary Reed--Solomon codes over prime fields, on arbitrary prescribed evaluation sets. For every fixed slack $γ>0$, every sufficiently large block length $n$, every prime $q\ge n$, and every dimension $1\le k\le(1-γ)n$, a deterministic algorithm finds all codewords within relative distance $1-k/n-γ$ in $q^{O_γ(1)}$ time. The final list has size $n^{O_γ(1)}$, independently of $q$. Both statements extend to bounded-input-list recovery, with constants depending additionally on the input-list bound. For every fixed curve degree $\ell$, at most $n^{O_{γ,\ell}(1)}$ parameters on a curve $f_0+zf_1+\cdots+z^\ell f_\ell$ admit a nearby codeword whose exact agreement support is not a maximal jointly explained support of the coefficient words. For lines this gives MCA error $n^{O_γ(1)}/q$, with no proximity loss. The interpolation stage reparameterizes and optimizes the hidden-derivative construction of Brakensiek, Chen, Putterman, Zhang, and Zheng; differential root enumeration uses Kopparty's algorithm. We then prove that a specialization-safe differential equation has a cover by constant-dimensional varieties of polynomial cumulative degree, outside polynomially many parameter values. Intersecting these varieties with equations from the full agreement support yields both the field-size-independent list bound and exact-support MCA.
paper.tldr: The interpolation stage reparameterizes and optimizes the hidden-derivative construction of Brakensiek, Chen, Putterman, Zhang, and Zheng; differential root enumeration uses Kopparty's algorithm.

paper.title: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
paper.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables object-level operations on Gaussian primitives, yet existing segmentation methods are largely trained and evaluated through rendered views. This mismatch can produce accurate rendered masks from incomplete 3D selections since alpha-blended feature supervision concentrates learning on dominant contributors while leaving occluded or low-contribution Gaussians weakly supervised. We propose VODA, a plug-and-play supervision objective that exploits local depth structure to group per-pixel contributors and directly supervises all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, bypassing contribution-weighted gradient delivery. To evaluate volumetric completeness, we introduce Removal-3D, a synthetic object-removal benchmark, and the Removal Depth Error (RDE), a metric comparing predicted and ground-truth depth changes. Across four rendering-based baselines, VODA consistently improves volumetric segmentation on Removal-3D while maintaining or improving performance on LERF and ScanNet. Further analysis shows that VODA recovers lower-contribution Gaussians, while simple gradient reweighting and spatial propagation fail to reproduce comparable gains.
paper.tldr: VODA consistently improves volumetric segmentation on Removal-3D while maintaining or improving performance on LERF and ScanNet, and shows that VODA recovers lower-contribution Gaussians, while simple gradient reweighting and spatial propagation fail to reproduce comparable gains.
